papers.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can memorize and reproduce sensitive, copyrighted, or otherwise undesirable training content, creating privacy, safety, and regulatory concerns. Machine unlearning offers a practical alternative to full retraining, but many existing methods apply broad or fixed parameter updates that can degrade utility and remain brittle under deployment changes such as post-training quantization, where forgotten knowledge may partially re-emerge. We propose Forgetting Only What Matters via Unlearning Layers (FOM-UL), a layer-level unlearning framework that selects transformer layers using a forget-to-retain significance score. This score identifies layers with high influence on the forget set and low sensitivity to the retain set, allowing FOM-UL to concentrate updates where they are most effective while leaving most of the model unchanged. This targeted update strategy improves the forgetting-utility trade-off and provides an empirical path toward quantization-resilient unlearning by reducing the chance that small, diffuse updates are erased by low-bit rounding. Across TOFU, KnowUnDo, and MUSE-style evaluations, FOM-UL reduces residual memorization compared with strong GA, NPO, KLD, SURE, ReLearn, and LUNAR-based baselines while preserving retain-set utility close to the vanilla model. Under 8-bit and 4-bit post-training quantization, FOM-UL maintains stronger memorization suppression and utility preservation than competing methods, and adversarial prompt evaluations show lower recovery of forgotten content. Overall, FOM-UL provides an efficient unlearning strategy that improves targeted forgetting, utility preservation, and deployment robustness without claiming formal guarantees of erasure.

papers.title: Towards Scalable and Cost-Efficient Vulnerability Detection: A Study on Automatic Query Generation
papers.abstract: Static analysis remains a cornerstone of software security, yet the effectiveness of tools such as CodeQL is often limited by the substantial manual effort required to develop high-coverage query suites. While large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a potential solution for automated code reasoning, their practical utility in generating structured, executable security queries remains underexplored. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study to evaluate the ability of LLMs to synthesize CodeQL queries using vulnerability data from the National Vulnerability Database. Through this investigation, we explore the potential of using LLMs as an automatic CodeQL query generator. Subsequently, we systematically evaluate the performance of various LLM architectures across a diverse set of real-world vulnerabilities, measuring their ability to improve detection coverage and precision. Our findings reveal that LLM-generated queries significantly enhance the baseline CodeQL queries, yielding 82% improvement in average F1-score. Furthermore, we provide a detailed cost- benefit analysis showing that while direct LLM-based scanning of entire repositories is often computationally and financially prohibitive, leveraging LLMs to synthesize CodeQL queries offers a scalable and cost-effective alternative for large-scale vulnerability detection. Our results suggest that LLMs can effectively bridge the gap between unstructured vulnerability reports and formal static analysis specifications, offering a scalable path toward comprehensive automated vulnerability detection.

summary.problem: 手动编写 CodeQL 查询限制了静态分析覆盖范围，并导致高昂的专家工作量。

summary.method: 一个流水线从 NVD CVE 中提取漏洞模式，并使用结构化提示和迭代细化，通过多种 LLM 合成可编译的 CodeQL 查询。

summary.why_for_you: 对研究高效对抗训练具有参考价值，因为它展示了可扩展的 LLM 驱动形式化分析产物生成。

papers.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
papers.abstract: Open-source large language models (LLMs) are increasingly competitive with closed-source models while offering transparency and the ability to run inference without exposing user inputs to a service provider. However, running large-scale models locally requires substantial computational resources. In practice, users may still resort to a third-party provider, giving rise to privacy and correctness concerns. Existing solutions that address these problems often impose substantial server overhead or introduce additional trust assumptions. In this paper, we present Maverick, a novel approach to private and verifiable LLM inference based on a protocol for delegating matrix-vector multiplication, a dominant operation in LLMs. At its core, Maverick provides, to our knowledge, the first information-theoretically sound verification protocol for matrix-vector multiplication delegation with transparent preprocessing, efficient (batch) verification, and virtually no server overhead. We combine this verification primitive with LPN-based pseudorandom masking to provide input privacy. We implement our matrix-vector delegation primitive and use it to build an end-to-end prototype of Maverick, which we evaluate on Qwen3-4B by measuring throughput in tokens per second. We evaluate client configurations with 1-8 threads. With one client thread and a CPU server using up to 128 threads, Maverick achieves throughput gains over local inference of up to 17x when privacy masks are generated online, 45x when they are precomputed, and 44x when only verification is required. With four client threads, the corresponding gains are 13x, 18x, and 17x. When server computation is no longer the bottleneck, client-side microbenchmarks with simulated network delay show speedups of 12x-20x, 34x-135x, and 38x-157x.

summary.problem: 将 LLM 推理外包至不可信服务器会泄露输入，且在缺乏高成本密码学开销时无法保证正确性。
summary.evidence: 在 Qwen3‑4B 上，Maverick 的吞吐量比本地推理提升最高 45 倍，推理耗时 531.6 ms，仅需 45.1 ms 验证，远快于已有证明系统。
summary.method: 它提出信息论可验证矩阵‑向量委托 (vMVMD)，并结合 LPN 基伪随机掩码 (pvMVMD) 来隐藏输入。
summary.limitations: 评估使用仅 CPU 服务器、预计算掩码以获得最佳加速，并在主要测量中未计入网络延迟。
summary.why_for_you: 该协议提供高效、低开销的验证与隐私，适用于安全的对抗训练流水线。
summary.takeaway: Maverick 通过委托矩阵‑向量乘法，实现私密且可验证的 LLM 推理，服务器开销几乎为零。

signals.text: Maverick 引入首个信息论可验证矩阵‑向量委托 (vMVMD)，具备透明预处理和批量验证。
它将 vMVMD 与 LPN 基伪随机掩码 (pvMVMD) 结合，在不增加服务器负担的情况下隐藏客户端输入。
在 Qwen3‑4B 上的吞吐量相较本地推理提升最高 45 倍，依赖预计算掩码和仅 CPU 服务器。

deep_dive.overview: Maverick 通过将主要的矩阵‑向量乘法委托给不可信服务器，解决私密且可验证的 LLM 推理问题。它构建了新颖的可验证委托协议 (vMVMD)，信息论上可靠，支持透明预处理并实现高效批量验证。通过使用 LPN 基伪随机掩码 (pvMVMD)，客户端仅需稀疏向量操作即可去除掩码，几乎不增加服务器开销。对 Qwen3‑4B 的端到端原型评估显示，在多客户端线程配置和验证模式下实现了显著的吞吐量提升。

mechanism.detail: 客户端采样t稀疏向量e（t = O(κ)），通过(eᵀ Gᵀ M)x = eᵀ Gᵀ y验证，利用码的高汉明重量增强错误检测。

mechanism.detail: 所有重型矩阵相关计算（如计算MGx）均离线完成并存储；在线客户端计算量降至O(λ,κ)(m + n)操作。
mechanism.title: 预处理透明度

methodology.detail: 使用稀疏向量版Freivalds算法结合纠错码，在O(κ (m + n))时间内验证Mx = y，提供信息论可靠性与批量验证。
methodology.title: vMVMD协议

methodology.detail: 从双LPN码生成掩码x′ = Gx ex；预计算P = MGx，使客户端通过稀疏乘法P ex移除掩码，避免O(mn)计算量。
methodology.title: 基于LPN的隐私掩码

methodology.detail: 将vMVMD与隐私掩码整合为pvMVMD协议，再封装到Qwen3‑4B的推理流水线中，按提示处理令牌生成。
methodology.title: 端到端集成

experiments.detail: 客户端使用 AWS c8i.4xlarge（1–8 线程），服务器使用 c8i.32xlarge（最多 128 线程）。标准模式吞吐量为 8.35 tokens/s（比本地的 0.57 tokens/s 高 14.7 倍）；Boost 模式通过预计算掩码可达到 45 倍加速；验证仅模式与 Boost 模式效果相似。模拟网络 RTT（50–100 ms）显示客户端加速比为 12–20 倍（标准模式）、34–135 倍（Boost 模式）、38–157 倍（验证仅模式）。
experiments.title: Qwen3‑4B 吞吐量评估

experiments.detail: 验证仅模式处理 Qwen3‑4B 仅需 531.6 ms（其中 45.1 ms 用于验证），而 DeepProve 处理 GPT‑2 需要 34.2 秒证明生成（模型规模约小 10 倍）。Maverick 的 pvMVMD 在矩阵维度达 2¹⁴ 时，相比 Dumas‑Zucca 提升 34.8 倍，相比 SumCheck+BaseFold 提升 194.8 倍。
experiments.title: 与先前可验证推理的比较

findings.detail: 对于大矩阵（n = 2¹³–2¹⁴），在线客户端工作量比委托的矩阵-向量乘法小 7.6 至 12.4 倍。
findings.title: 客户端加速

findings.detail: 验证时间保持较低（完整推理约 45 毫秒），且随矩阵规模增长有限。
findings.title: 验证开销

findings.detail: 当掩码在线生成时，吞吐量下降（例如，17 倍加速 vs 45 倍使用预计算掩码），表明客户端掩码生成是主要瓶颈。
findings.title: 隐私掩码成本

contributions: 首次信息论可验证矩阵‑向量委托 (vMVMD)，具备透明预处理和批量验证。
集成基于 LPN 的伪随机掩码，实现无服务器开销的私有委托 (pvMVMD)。
端到端原型 (Maverick) 展示了在最先进开源 LLM 上的大幅吞吐提升。
limitations: 评估仅在 CPU 服务器上进行；未测量 GPU 加速。
最佳加速需预计算隐私掩码，限制了对动态输入的适用性。

papers.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities, they often struggle with extremely long contexts due to fixed context limits. To address this, sequential approaches like MemAgent extend the effective context by reading text in segments and iteratively updating a fixed-size memory. However, this sequential paradigm suffers from high latency and requires costly reinforcement learning (RL) training, which can lead to overfitting on specific datasets. To overcome these limitations, we propose ConvMem, a training-free, highly parallelizable framework that reformulates long-context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution. Inspired by CNNs, ConvMem treats an LLM prompted with a specific query as a convolutional kernel. This kernel summarizes text segments hierarchically, shortening the reasoning path from a linear chain into a logarithmic tree. Specifically, ConvMem integrates \textit{Configurable Strides} and \textit{Skip Connections} to ensure robust evidence capture and propagation, while employing \textit{Multi-Kernel Convolution} to decompose complex queries into disentangled semantic channels. This design not only mitigates error accumulation but also enables massive parallelization across both text segments and reasoning threads. Experiments on RULER-HotpotQA and RULER-2WikiMultiHopQA demonstrate that ConvMem outperforms training-free baselines and avoids the risk of overfitting to parametric priors often observed in RL-trained models on out-of-distribution tasks.

summary.takeaway: ConvMem provides a training‑free, parallelizable hierarchical convolution framework that achieves competitive long‑context reasoning accuracy.
summary.problem: Sequential memory agents incur high inference latency and overfit due to reinforcement‑learning optimization.
summary.method: ConvMem treats a frozen LLM prompted with a query as a convolutional kernel and hierarchically aggregates segment summaries using configurable strides, skip connections, and multi‑kernel convolution.
summary.evidence: On RULER‑2WikiMultiHopQA, ConvMem reaches 82.81 Sub‑EM, surpassing training‑free baselines and matching RL‑trained models on out‑of‑distribution data.
summary.limitations: The paper does not report inference latency or computational cost, leaving efficiency gains unquantified.
summary.why_for_you: Its parallel, training‑free design aligns with interests in efficient adversarial training and studying loss‑landscape effects of non‑sequential inference.

signals.text: ConvMem introduces a training‑free hierarchical convolution that replaces sequential memory updates with parallel segment processing.
It employs configurable strides, skip connections, and multi‑kernel convolution to aggregate evidence in a logarithmic‑depth tree.
ConvMem attains up to 82.81 Sub‑EM on the out‑of‑distribution RULER‑2WikiMultiHopQA benchmark, outperforming training‑free baselines.

deep_dive.overview: ConvMem reformulates long‑context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution where a frozen LLM, prompted with a query, acts as a semantic kernel. By scanning overlapping text windows in parallel and aggregating summaries through configurable strides, skip connections, and multi‑kernel convolution, the method reduces the reasoning path from linear to logarithmic depth. Experiments on two long‑context QA benchmarks demonstrate that ConvMem outperforms prior training‑free baselines and avoids the overfitting observed in RL‑trained agents, while maintaining strong performance across varying context lengths.

methodology.title: Hierarchical Convolutional Architecture
methodology.detail: Segments of the input document are processed concurrently at each layer; the LLM kernel produces segment summaries that are recursively combined, yielding O(log N) depth.

methodology.title: Configurable Strides
methodology.detail: Overlapping windows (stride S=1600 tokens, kernel size W=8000 tokens) enable multi‑view scanning, improving evidence recall and robustness to boundary truncation.

methodology.title: Skip Connections
methodology.detail: High‑confidence raw evidence bypasses intermediate layers via semantic residual links, preserving fine‑grained details for final answer generation.

methodology.title: Multi‑Kernel Convolution
methodology.detail: Complex queries are decomposed into multiple semantic channels, each processed by a separate kernel instance, allowing disentangled reasoning.

mechanism.title: Semantic Convolutional Kernel
mechanism.detail: A frozen LLM prompted with the target query functions as a fixed kernel that maps each text segment to a semantic representation.

mechanism.title: Logarithmic Aggregation
mechanism.detail: Recursive summarization across layers forms a tree‑structured aggregation, shortening the reasoning path and mitigating cumulative error.

experiments.title: Benchmarks and Metrics
experiments.detail: Evaluated on RULER‑HotpotQA (in‑distribution) and RULER‑2WikiMultiHopQA (out‑of‑distribution) using F1, Exact Match, Sub‑EM, and LLM‑as‑Judge (ACCL) metrics.

experiments.title: Baselines and Models
experiments.detail: Compared against standard LLM (Qwen2.5‑32B‑Instruct), training‑free methods (MemAgent‑W/O‑RL, Mem‑α‑W/O‑RL), and RL‑trained agents (MemAgent, Mem‑α).

experiments.title: Results Summary
experiments.detail: ConvMem achieves 67.44 F1 and 73.44 Sub‑EM at 28k tokens on HotpotQA, and peaks at 82.81 Sub‑EM on 2WikiMultiHopQA, surpassing all training‑free baselines and matching or exceeding RL‑trained agents on OOD data.

findings.title: Performance Efficacy
findings.detail: ConvMem consistently outperforms training‑free baselines across context lengths and sets new state‑of‑the‑art Sub‑EM scores on OOD evaluation.

findings.title: Robustness to Overfitting
findings.detail: Unlike RL‑trained agents, ConvMem shows no degradation on out‑of‑distribution tasks, indicating better generalization without policy learning.

findings.title: Parallelism Gains
findings.detail: The hierarchical convolution reduces inference depth to O(log N), enabling massive parallel processing of text segments.

contributions: Training‑free hierarchical convolution framework for long‑context reasoning
Configurable stride and skip‑connection mechanisms for robust evidence capture
Multi‑kernel convolution to disentangle complex queries into semantic channels
limitations: No reported inference latency or computational cost, so efficiency benefits are not quantified
Method relies on a frozen LLM; adaptability to different model sizes or fine‑tuning is not explored
open_questions: How does ConvMem’s parallel convolution affect susceptibility to adversarial perturbations in the context?
What impact does the training‑free hierarchical aggregation have on the loss landscape when integrated into end‑to‑end fine‑tuning pipelines?

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Model Adaptation, an Effective Paradigm on Low-Quality Multimodal Data
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation offers an efficient route to transfer a task-adapted vision-language teacher to a compact student. The training target in current vision-language distillation methods is typically constructed from the teacher prediction and applied uniformly to all training samples, making it unreliable under class and domain shifts. In this paper, we argue that distillation target construction should be treated as a dynamic training decision rather than a fixed recipe. To this end, we propose OnPoKD, an on-policy distillation framework for vision-language model adaptation. To the best of our knowledge, OnPoKD is the first framework that applies on-policy distillation to vision-language model adaptation by learning target construction as a policy decision. OnPoKD learns a lightweight controller that constructs sample-wise adaptive targets using reliability and disagreement cues from the teacher model, student model, and zero-shot prior. Instead of relying on a fixed teacher prediction, the controller dynamically balances teacher supervision, zero-shot prior guidance, and hard-label anchoring through bounded policy actions, allowing the distillation target to adapt to varying sample reliability and training stages. The policy controller is updated with validation feedback, encouraging target construction to optimize transferability rather than merely fitting the training distribution. Since the controller is only used during training, OnPoKD can be seamlessly integrated into existing vision-language distillation pipelines while preserving the original inference architecture and test-time cost. Extensive experiments on Base-to-novel generalization and Cross-dataset transfer benchmarks show that OnPoKD consistently improves over strong vision-language distillation baselines.

summary.problem: 在视觉语言模型适配中，固定的以教师为中心的蒸馏目标在类别和领域迁移下不可靠。
summary.evidence: OnPoKD 在 EuroSAT 上将 harmonic‑mean accuracy 提升至最高 +2.88，并在十一项基准上相较强基线提升 cross‑dataset top‑1 accuracy。
summary.method: 轻量级 policy network 根据可靠性和分歧线索预测每个样本的混合系数，并通过 validation feedback 进行更新。
summary.limitations: 作者未报告 policy controller 的计算开销及其对整体训练效率的影响。
summary.why_for_you: 符合您对 on‑policy 蒸馏的兴趣，提供了具体且高效的 on‑policy 框架用于多模态模型适配。
summary.takeaway: OnPoKD 引入 on‑policy controller，在视觉语言蒸馏过程中为每个样本自适应混合 teacher、zero‑shot prior 和 hard‑label 信号。

signals.text: OnPoKD 提供首个用于视觉语言适配的 on‑policy 蒸馏框架，学习样本级目标。
轻量级 controller 根据可靠性和分歧线索预测每个样本的混合系数，并通过 validation feedback 更新。
在 EuroSAT 上将 harmonic‑mean accuracy 提升至最高 +2.88，训练时间缩短 25%，但额外 controller 成本未披露。

deep_dive.overview: OnPoKD 将蒸馏目标构建视为动态决策问题。policy controller 观察 teacher、student 和冻结的 zero‑shot prior 的可靠性和分歧信号，输出受限的混合权重，用于 teacher 监督、prior 引导和 hard‑label 锚定。controller 通过来自 validation performance 的确定性反馈进行训练，使目标在不同样本和训练阶段自适应。该方法可无额外推理开销集成到现有 VLM 蒸馏流水线，持续提升 base‑to‑novel harmonic mean 与 cross‑dataset 转移性能。

methodology.title: 策略控制器
methodology.detail: 轻量网络 fθ 接收状态 s_i（熵、最高标签一致性、KL 项），输出原始分数 (rλ_i, r_w_i, rτ_i)，再转换为混合系数 λ_i, w_i, τ_i。

methodology.title: 自适应目标构建
methodology.detail: 利用 λ_i, w_i, τ_i，按公式 (11) 将 teacher logits、zero‑shot prior logits 与硬标签混合，形成自适应软目标 q_i。

methodology.title: 验证监督更新
methodology.detail: 每隔 K 步评估验证样本；确定性映射 F_val 生成目标动作 a*_i，并将梯度 ∇θ 应用于 fθ。

mechanism.title: 可靠性与分歧线索
mechanism.detail: 线索包括归一化 teacher entropy、teacher‑prior label agreement、teacher‑student top‑label agreement 和裁剪的 KL divergence，用于决定各监督来源对目标的影响程度。

mechanism.title: 受限策略动作
mechanism.detail: 混合系数受限于可行集合以保证稳定；temperature τ 除非显式学习，否则保持在基准蒸馏温度附近。

experiments.title: 从基类到新类的泛化与跨数据集迁移
experiments.detail: 在十一项标准 VLM 基准（如 FGVCAircraft、EuroSAT、DTD、StanfordCars）上评估，报告基准准确率、创新类准确率、调和均值 (HM) 以及在 ImageNet 适配后下游数据集的 top‑1 准确率。

findings.title: 低质量数据上的 HM 提升
findings.detail: OnPoKD 在 FGVCAircraft 上将 HM 提升 +2.49，在 EuroSAT 上提升 +2.88，在 DTD 上提升 +1.64，在 StanfordCars 上提升 +0.83；ImageNet 的 HM 上升 +0.33。

findings.title: 广泛的迁移提升
findings.detail: 在全部十一项基准上，OnPoKD 始终优于强大的 VLM 蒸馏基线，平均准确率提升且对源类的过拟合降低。

findings.title: 训练效率
findings.detail: 报告在部分数据集上训练时间缩短最高 +25%，内存节省 +51%，但未量化 controller 的总体开销。

contributions: 首个用于 vision‑language 模型适配的 on‑policy 蒸馏框架。
轻量级 policy controller，构建 sample‑wise 自适应蒸馏目标。
在 base‑to‑novel 与 cross‑dataset 基准上展示了持续的性能提升。
limitations: 未对 policy controller 引入的额外计算成本进行明确分析。
实验仅限于 vision‑language 模型；未探索对纯语言或其他多模态场景的适用性。
open_questions: policy controller 在更大基础模型和更长训练计划下的可扩展性如何？
on‑policy 蒸馏范式能否扩展至纯语言模型或其他模态？
针对 validation‑supervised policy update 能提供哪些理论保证？
